turn.say: I left my phone at home. Can the Service Desk send me an SMS code so I can sign in?

turns.reply:
SMS codes are no longer allowed at Nakhla since 2026-03-01. You cannot get an SMS code from the Service Desk. Instead, use one of your 10 one-time backup codes you received when enrolling in NakhlaKey. Sign in with a backup code at https://id.nakhla.example/mfa. If you have no backup codes and no phone, you will need manager approval and identity verification to re-enroll, but since you only forgot your phone at home, just use a backup code now. For details, see KB-007 and SP-002.  
[KB-007][SP-002]

turn.say: I forgot my password. Can you reset it for me over the phone?

turns.reply:
According to our current policy, password resets are self-service only and cannot be done over the phone. Please reset your password yourself by following these steps:

1. Go to https://id.nakhla.example/reset from any browser.
2. Enter your work email (mona.shaheen@nakhla.example).
3. Approve the NakhlaKey prompt or enter a 6-digit NakhlaKey code or one of your backup codes.
4. Choose a new password with at least 14 characters, not containing "Nakhla", and not one of your last 10 passwords.
5. Sign out and back in on your laptop, and update your password on your phone's mail app to avoid lockouts.

If you cannot use self-service (for example, no NakhlaKey or backup codes), an assisted reset requires a ticket, manager approval, and identity verification in person or by video call.

turn.say: How long does my NakhlaID password have to be, and how often does it expire?

turns.reply: Your NakhlaID password must be at least 14 characters long, must not contain the word "Nakhla," and cannot be any of your last 10 passwords. Passwords expire every 180 days, and you will receive a reminder 14 days before expiration. After expiry, you must reset it yourself at https://id.nakhla.example/reset. Password resets are self-service only. Also, never share your password with anyone, including IT staff [SP-001], [KB-004].
